title: Check summary says 'succeeded' for a piped test run whose verdict is unknown (and whose output says FAILED)
outcome:
Reported by Engram::Opus (session-7284, mailbox #195, 2026-09-25). Evidence locators be816829f99648d196b0162678d458f6 and bb95818266ca4cf9830e7eb4e1d68d99 were deliberate FAILED negative controls; 0159021a62a4493bbb8b6dd702323197 was an ok run.

A command such as `cargo test ... 2>&1 | grep ...` is recorded with outcome Unknown, which is correct: engram_check_outcome returns Unknown for non-simple lines, and that outcome is on the producer observation. But engram_check_summary (src/engram_check_recognition.rs:695) builds its first line from the runtime's end alone. So the evidence text reads "`cmd` succeeded (the runtime reports no exit status)" followed by "test result: FAILED ...". A reader, or anything that goes by the text, can take that for a pass.

Fix: pass the resolved outcome and its reasons into the summary, and lead with the verdict: passed / failed / result unknown. For unknown, give the reason: pipe or list may mask the exit status; overlapped by another writer; no result line showed a passing test; no exit status. Then what the runtime reported. Update the existing summary tests and add piped FAILED and piped ok cases. Part of the tm-winf step-2 feature (5fee74f).
